title: The Matrix
logline: A hacker who senses that the world is wrong is shown that it is a machine-farmed dream, and must choose between the safety of ignorance and a cause worth dying for — a choice that ends with him refusing the death the system pronounces for him.
premise: A man raised inside a lie is told the truth will free him, but the truth is unbearable and the freedom costs everyone around him their lives — so he must decide whether to believe in himself enough to die for a man he cannot save by any logic.
audience: viewers who want a story where the spectacle (rooftop chases, kung-fu, bullet-stopping) is the physical expression of a question about what is real and whether choice can override a written fate
setting: a dual world — a neural-interactive simulation styled as a late-1990s city, and the ruined real Earth of ~2197 where the last free humans live aboard a hovercraft in the sewers
pov: third-person objective on the page, but experientially anchored to Neo — the world is revealed as he is told it, and the camera returns to him alone (the subway, the hallway) at the two places where belief must be chosen
style: lean, procedural action described as cause-and-effect chains (a package rings, a voice guides, a mouth seals), with reality-bending rendered as physical fact rather than explanation; dialogue carries the philosophy while the images carry the cost

narrative_vector.goal: to reach the truth of the Matrix and become the One
narrative_vector.motivation: a lifelong, nameless dread that the world is wrong, and a refusal to accept the fate the system assigns him
narrative_vector.conflict: the Machines hunt him as a threat while his own disbelief tells him he is not the One
narrative_vector.generative_question: What if the world you trust is a lie, and the only way out is to believe something you cannot prove?

audiences.why_this_group: The film delivers a high-concept chase-and-combat engine — rooftop leaps, kung-fu downloads, a helicopter rescue, a subway brawl, bullet-stopping — that runs from the first scene to the last.
audiences.reader_promise: You will get escalating, physics-defying set pieces, each one tied to a rule of the world you just learned (Agents match leaps, the mind bends rules, death in the Matrix kills the body).

audiences.why_this_group: The plot is built as a live argument about simulation, free will, and the cost of truth, staged through the red-pill choice and Cypher's counter-argument.
audiences.reader_promise: You will get a story that treats 'is reality real?' and 'do we choose or is it written?' as the actual engine of the plot, not decoration.

audiences.why_this_group: Neo is a double-life hacker who is told his real name is a lie and a new one is pressed onto him before he has earned it — an identity story anyone who has felt out of place can enter.
audiences.reader_promise: You will get a protagonist whose awakening from a hollow, deferential routine into a self-chosen purpose mirrors the feeling of finally becoming who you were told you could not be.

rules_of_the_world: The perceived world is a neural-interactive simulation (the Matrix); the real world is a ruined Earth around 2197. This is obeyed: Neo is shown the 'desert of the real' and told the year is not 1997.

Humans are grown in pods and hardwired into the Matrix; freeing a mind requires locating and unplugging them. Obeyed: Neo is unjacked via the coaxial cable at his skull and nearly drowns before recovery.

A hardline phone inside the Matrix is an exit to the real world; once a line is traced it becomes unusable and dangerous. Obeyed: Trinity's line is cut (ev-003), the office phone becomes a raid trigger (ev-006), and Neo escapes only through a ringing phone (ev-046).

Agents are sentient programs that can move into any still-hardwired human and can override physics (seal a mouth, match a 40-foot leap). Obeyed: Smith seals Neo's mouth (ev-007) and Brown duplicates Trinity's leap (ev-003); anyone unplugged is 'potentially an Agent.'

Death inside the Matrix kills the real body. Obeyed: Mouse stays dead (ev-023) and Apoc and Switch die when unplugged during Cypher's betrayal (ev-029) — the rule that makes Neo's death-and-revival a violation rather than a trick.

The mind governs the simulation: rules 'can be bent' or 'broken' once a person stops believing them ('know,' don't 'try'). Obeyed: Neo downloads kung fu (ev-015), fails the jump because he doubts (ev-016), and finally stops bullets by believing (ev-045).

The Construct is a loading program where anything — clothes, weapons, training — can be inserted, and appearance there is a 'residual self image.' Obeyed: Morpheus loads the dojo, the jump program, and the crowded-street Agent lesson (ev-015, ev-016, ev-018).

A deja vu signals a glitch where the machines have changed something in the Matrix. Obeyed: the repeated cat exposes the rewrite that springs the Hotel Lafayette trap (ev-023).  [TESTED — it is the warning that the trap has closed.]
forbidden_tics: It avoids voice-over or expository narration — the world is explained only through in-world dialogue (Morpheus's lessons, Smith's interrogation), never an authorial aside.
It avoids treating reality-bending as spectacle-for-its-own-sake; every impossible feat is paid for by a rule of the world and a cost (doubt injures Neo, death is real).
It avoids a tidy, guaranteed hero — the protagonist repeatedly fails (beaten in the dojo, falls off the rooftop, dies) and denies his own destiny rather than strutting into it.
It avoids making the comfortable lie a straw villain — Cypher's case for ignorance is given its most sensual, defensible moment (the steak, the wine) before it turns murderous.
It avoids resolving the central faith question with proof — Morpheus reinterprets prophecy and silence as confirmation rather than producing evidence, and Neo acts before he believes.

identification_value.admirable_strength: a refusal to accept an assigned fate — even at the point of death, when Smith pronounces his name and inevitability, Neo answers 'My name... is Neo' and summons a surge that breaks the predicted outcome.
identification_value.opening_vulnerability: the private, nameless dread that the world is wrong, paired with a deferential, hollow compliance to authority (he answers his boss's ultimatum with flat politeness and curses the alarm clock) — a feeling of being trapped in a life that isn't real that most people recognise.
identification_value.connection: the same refusal-to-accept that makes him admirable is what makes his ordinary life unbearable in the first place — his dissatisfaction is the price of the honesty that later lets him see through the Matrix, and it costs him his entire former identity (captured, mouth sealed, bug implanted, ejected from the pod).

entity_roster.name: Neo / Thomas A. Anderson
entity_roster.description: A hacker living a double life — 'Thomas A. Anderson' by day at Meta CorTechs, 'Neo' in computers — who is hunted, implanted with a tracker, unplugged from a growth pod, and told he is the prophesied One he does not believe he is.

entity_roster.name: Trinity
entity_roster.description: A freed crew member and the film's opening action figure who extracts Neo, removes his bug, and — as her private faith in him grows — refuses his death and revives him with a declaration of love, then becomes the ranking officer who commands the rescue.

entity_roster.name: Morpheus
entity_roster.description: The captain of the Nebuchadnezzar who is certain Neo is the One, reveals the truth of the Matrix, is captured and tortured for the Zion access codes, and whose near-death is what forces Neo's wager to rescue him.

entity_roster.name: Tank
entity_roster.description: The Nebuchadnezzar's operator who guides the crew by voice, is shot and left for dead by Cypher, and survives to kill Cypher and steer the final escape.

entity_roster.name: Agent Smith
entity_roster.description: The system's most committed enforcer — a sentient program who seals mouths, hunts Neo personally with disgust-tinged obsession, tortures Morpheus, shoots Neo dead in the hallway, and is finally destroyed from within when Neo bursts out of him.

entity_roster.name: Cypher / Mr. Reagan
entity_roster.description: A resentful crew insider who bargains with Agent Smith to be reinserted into the Matrix in exchange for the Zion codes, drops a phone to spring the Hotel Lafayette trap, and murders Apoc, Switch and Dozer before being killed by Tank.

entity_roster.name: The Agents (Brown and Jones)
entity_roster.description: The collective of sentient-program enforcers who hunt the freed crew, breach rooms, match impossible leaps, and — after Neo destroys Smith — feel fear for the first time.

entity_roster.name: The Nebuchadnezzar (the ship)
entity_roster.description: The hovercraft the freed crew lives and operates from in the real-world sewers; it carries the operator chair and screens, the EMP weapon, and the harnesses the crew jacks into — and its hull is breached by Sentinels at the climax.

entity_roster.name: The Matrix (the simulation)
entity_roster.description: The machine-built neural-interactive dreamworld that farms humans for power; it can be rewritten (deja vu), bent or broken by those who stop believing its rules, and serves as the entire battleground of the plot.

entity_roster.name: The Sentinels / machines
entity_roster.description: The real-world mechanical hunters that sweep the sewers, force the ship to hide and arm its EMP, and overrun the deck as Neo dies — the physical survival threat running parallel to the Matrix war.

entity_roster.name: The hardline phone (exit)
entity_roster.description: The ringing landline inside the Matrix that serves as the only way back to the real world; it is cut, traced, and weaponised by the plot, and Neo's final escape depends on reaching one before Smith's bullet lands.

entity_roster.name: The red pill / blue pill
entity_roster.description: Morpheus's offered choice — the blue pill to forget and the red pill, part of a trace program, to know — the single act that commits Neo to the truth and sets the whole story in motion.

plot_briefs.name: Neo's awakening and initiation
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Neo wants the truth behind the lifelong dread that the world is wrong, so he follows the white rabbit and, when offered the choice, swallows the red pill.
plot_briefs.what_resists: His own attachment to the safe double life (he plans to work the next day), the Agents who capture and bug him, and the unbearable physical truth of the real world that makes him recoil.
plot_briefs.cost: His entire former identity is destroyed — captured, mouth sealed, tracker implanted, ejected naked from a growth pod and nearly drowned.
plot_briefs.resolution: He is recovered aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, rebuilt, and shown the truth of the Matrix, accepting there is no going back.

plot_briefs.name: Becoming the One (training and the Oracle)
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Morpheus wants to confirm Neo as the prophesied One who will end the war, so he trains him and takes him to the Oracle.
plot_briefs.what_resists: Neo's disbelief (he is beaten in the dojo, fails the rooftop jump, and says 'I don't believe in anything anymore') and the Oracle's private verdict, which Neo is ordered to keep secret.
plot_briefs.cost: Repeated physical failure and injury, and a death-prophecy he must carry alone.
plot_briefs.resolution: The trip to the Oracle springs the Agents' trap, killing Mouse and capturing Morpheus — converting the abstract question of belief into a concrete, fatal choice.

plot_briefs.name: Cypher's betrayal
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Cypher wants to escape the hardship of the real world, so he bargains with Agent Smith to be reinserted into the Matrix in exchange for the Zion mainframe codes.
plot_briefs.what_resists: The crew he must murder to deliver on the deal — he shoots Tank, kills Apoc and Switch, and hands Morpheus to the Agents.
plot_briefs.cost: He becomes a murderer of his own comrades and is himself struck down by Tank, whom he had left for dead.
plot_briefs.resolution: Tank survives and kills Cypher, but Morpheus is already delivered to the Agents for torture.

plot_briefs.name: The rescue of Morpheus
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Neo — denying he is the One — wants to bring Morpheus back alive rather than let the crew pull the plug, so he goes back into the Matrix with Trinity.
plot_briefs.what_resists: The logic that Morpheus is already lost (a wager on a man, not a prophecy), the Agents holding him, and the building's guards.
plot_briefs.cost: Any claim to safety; the mission carries no prophetic guarantee, only faith.
plot_briefs.resolution: They storm the government building, helicopter-extract Morpheus, and escape — during which Trinity confesses the Oracle told her she would fall in love with the One, and that man is Neo.

plot_briefs.name: Neo vs. Smith and the final escape
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Trapped alone in the subway, Neo chooses to stand and fight Agent Smith rather than flee, and the crew must get everyone out before the Sentinels destroy the ship.
plot_briefs.what_resists: Smith, who frames Neo's death as settled inevitability and shoots him dead in the hotel hallway, while Sentinels breach the hull in the real world.
plot_briefs.cost: Neo dies — shot three times, monitors flatline — and is revived only by Trinity's refusal to accept the ending.
plot_briefs.resolution: Revived, Neo reads the Matrix as code, stops bullets, and destroys Smith from within; he escapes through a ringing phone as Morpheus detonates the EMP, saving the ship — then, as the fully realised One, calls the machines and flies off.

turning_points.name: The red pill — committing to the truth
turning_points.where: Act I turn, after Neo is drawn through the white rabbit, captured and bugged by the Agents, and offered the choice between forgetting and knowing; he swallows the red pill (ev-010).  [Sits early, once the ordinary world has been shown and the threat made real.]

turning_points.name: The trap springs — Morpheus captured
turning_points.where: Act II midpoint/turn, when the deja vu exposes the Matrix being rewritten, Mouse is killed, the crew is sealed in the Hotel Lafayette, and Morpheus sacrifices his freedom so Neo can escape (ev-023, ev-025, ev-026).  [Sits at the centre, converting belief from theory to a fatal stake.]

turning_points.name: Cypher's betrayal — the crew nearly destroyed
turning_points.where: Late Act II, when Cypher murders Dozer, Apoc and Switch and delivers Morpheus to the Agents, only to be killed by the surviving Tank (ev-029).  [Sits just before the rescue, stripping the crew to Neo and Trinity.]

turning_points.name: The rescue wager — choosing a man over a prophecy
turning_points.where: Act II→III turn, when Neo stops Morpheus's plug from being pulled and commits to going back in despite denying he is the One, with Trinity joining as ranking officer (ev-032).  [Sits at the launch of the final movement.]

turning_points.name: Death, revival, and the One awakened
turning_points.where: Act III climax, when Smith shoots Neo dead in the hallway, Trinity revives him, and Neo stops bullets and destroys Smith, then escapes as the EMP saves the ship (ev-044, ev-045, ev-046).  [Sits at the peak, resolving the identity and faith questions by action rather than proof.]

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: Know an unbearable reality — Neo takes the red pill and recoils at the farmed, ruined truth, but gains a cause worth dying for.
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Live a pleasant illusion — Cypher savours an impossible steak and bargains to be re-plugged, choosing ignorant comfort over painful freedom.
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: The red-pill choice (ev-010), the 'Desert of the Real' revelation (ev-013), and Cypher's steak-and-Smith bargain (ev-020).

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: Cut the loss and escape — the rational, survivable move when Morpheus is taken, the crew's own default of pulling his plug.
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Risk everything to save one man you cannot save by logic — Neo goes back in, a wager on a man rather than a prophecy.
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: The central dilemma: Morpheus already modeled sacrifice by giving his life for Neo (ev-025), Cypher modeled self-preservation by betraying him (ev-020), and Neo's rescue wager resolves it (ev-032).

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: The path is written — the Oracle's prophecy and verdict set up a pre-scripted destiny that even Neo is ordered to accept.
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Choice overrides destiny — Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces at the point of death and summons a surge that breaks the predicted outcome.
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: The prophecy of the One (ev-014), the Oracle's private verdict (ev-023), and Neo's subway refusal and revival (ev-039, ev-044).

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: A life of purposeful struggle — Neo moves from the hollow, deferential routine of Meta CorTechs toward a cause worth dying for.
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Empty satisfaction — Cypher recasts the cause as a body count and trades hard, meaningful freedom for soft, meaningless comfort.
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: Neo's mundane office ultimatum (ev-005), Cypher's 'body count' speech and steak (ev-020), and Neo's rescue commitment (ev-032).

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: Death is final — Mouse, Apoc, Switch and Dozer die and stay dead, giving mortality its weight.
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Death is a boundary the awakened can contest — Neo is shot three times and confirmed gone, then called back to life.
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: The permanent deaths of Mouse (ev-023) and the betrayed crew (ev-029) set against Neo's death and Trinity's reviving kiss (ev-044, ev-045).

state_dimensions: The story's emotional weather moves from dread and confinement (the gutted hotel, the sealed office, the pod) through disorientation and violation (the real world, the bug, the torture) to grief (the dead crew) and finally to release and transcendence (revival, the kiss, flight).

Its moral temperature rises as belief is tested: from the comfortable lie, through the painful truth, to a faith that acts without proof — culminating in a choice that costs the hero his life and returns it transformed.

The tension is engineered as a ratchet: every escape tightens the next trap (the cut hardline, the dropped phone, the breached hull), so relief is always short and the stakes compound until the final, simultaneous Matrix-and-real-world climax.
constraints: Every claim must be grounded in the provided event layer, spine facts, meta layer or entity roster — no scene, character or event is invented beyond them.
The world's rules are obeyed as stated (death is real, phones are exits, Agents override physics, the mind bends rules) so that Neo's revival reads as a violation of a priced-in rule, not a loophole.
The identity and faith questions are resolved by action and choice, never by produced proof — Morpheus reinterprets prophecy and silence; Neo believes by acting.
keep_in_mind: Neo's arc is belief-before-power: he fails physically every time he doubts and only succeeds when he stops trying and knows.
Trinity's arc is grief-into-command: her private faith, not the prophecy, is what actually revives Neo and leads the rescue.
Cypher is the film's defensible counter-argument made flesh — his case for ignorance is given its most sensual moment before it turns to murder, so he is never a straw villain.
The two places the story isolates Neo alone — the subway and the hotel hallway — are where belief must be chosen, and both are answered by refusing the fate the system pronounces.
